body.statement: There exist constants \(c,C,c_1,C_1>0\), depending only on \(\Delta_0,b_0,M,\sigma,\delta\) and the context-density constants, such that for \(C_1\log T\le\rho\le c_1T\), \(c\rho^{-1/2}\le W_{T,\delta}(\rho;\mathcal P_{\Delta_0,b_0}^{\mathrm{fg}})\le C\rho^{-1/2}\). The lower inequality holds for every non-anticipating design and every honest interval. The upper inequality is attained by an explicit explore-then-track design that learns the gap sign, spends the remaining budget on the inferior treatment, and reports one connected predictably weighted interval. Relative to SimchiLeviWang2023BanditExperimentalDesign, this is a strict strengthening from point-estimator error for a noncontextual treatment-effect gap to all honest intervals for the nonlinear contextual targeting gain with a \(P\)-independent benchmark.
body.justification: This theorem isolates the compulsory \(\rho^{-1/2}\) obstruction and verifies that benchmark cancellation cannot remove it.
body.gap: SimchiLeviWang2023BanditExperimentalDesign matches regret and treatment-effect estimation error for finite arms, while HadadEtAl2021AdaptiveConfidenceIntervals treats fixed-arm means under supplied adaptive propensities; neither gives an all-procedure honest-width statement for this causal gain.
body.consumer: Trialists using a conventional benchmark obtain the exact price of protecting participants away from treatment ties and a design that pays no additional order penalty.
